facts.F1:
ADO User Story 6712 "Faster page loads on slow connections: compression, shared cache, smaller update check", as written on the board:

On a slow connection, Lighthouse pages take 8–20 s to show their data on a first visit, and 5–9 s when you click to a Team or Portfolio page. A measuring spike (2026-11-27, docs/feature/api-shape-evaluation/spike/findings.md) found that most of that time is spent sending uncompressed JavaScript, not on the number of API calls.

Fixes found by the spike
- Compression. The frontend is served with UseStaticFiles, which ignores the .gz files the build already makes, and API answers are not compressed. JavaScript: 3.4 MB raw vs 1.0 MB compressed. Expected gain on slow 4G: about 4–10 s per page.
- One shared cache for data every page uses. useRbac fetches the user's permissions once per component that uses it (72 repeated calls over 16 pages). Teams, portfolios, licence and Team settings repeat for similar reasons.
- A smaller update check. GET /version/new sends 368 KB of release notes on every first visit, only to show whether an update exists.
- Parallel version checks. The version footer runs 5 independent checks one after another.

No visible UI change; pages show the same data, sooner. Measure before and after with the spike's probe (measure-calls.mjs, measure-bytes.mjs).

Separate from the GraphQL / API-shape evaluation, which continues on its own and ends in an ADR.

facts.F648: Page-move freshness (S2, S3): one owner, usePageFreshQuery in src/hooks/usePageFreshQuery.ts, wraps useQuery with staleTime Infinity and retry false. Its queryFn returns the answer with the page it was asked on (carrier PageFreshAnswer of T: answer and askedOnPage) and on failure throws PageFreshFailure carrying askedOnPage; TanStack keeps the last good data when a later ask fails. refetchOnMount is a function: a mounting component asks only when no request is in flight and the latest settled ask (data or error) was asked on an earlier page than the current one, so a reader that mounts after a page with no reader asks once instead of waiting for ever; refetchType all was rejected because it would ask on pages that have no reader. PageMoveRefresh in src/components/App/PageMoveRefresh/PageMoveRefresh.tsx, mounted inside the Router in App.tsx, holds the page counter (per-process state, a React context) and the last pathname together in one useState value { lastPathname, page }, never in a ref or module variable. During render, only when location.pathname differs from lastPathname, it sets that value to { pathname, page + 1 } in one update, so a StrictMode double render or an abandoned concurrent render cannot advance one without the other or lose a move, and a component that first renders under the new path already reads the new page. In an effect keyed on page it invalidates the shared page reads once (invalidateQueries cancels a request still in flight and refetches the active queries). The own-change refresh (useRefreshPermissions, useUnitListsChanged) invalidates with refetchType all, so it asks once even when no reader is mounted. Each component records its mount page once, in a useState initializer, on its first render. React keeps a component of the same type in the same place mounted across a route change; such a component keeps its earlier mount page. Readiness per component: ready when the last good answer was asked on or after its mount page, whatever happened to later asks; failed when it has no such answer, nothing is in flight and the latest ask failed (the permissive fallback with loadFailed true); loading otherwise. Readiness is never decided by the page the user is on now. Consequences: a component that shows an answer and stays mounted keeps showing it, not loading and not the fallback, while a page-move or own-change ask runs and when that ask fails (today such a component never asked again, so a failure never touched it); it switches when a new good answer lands. A component that mounts on the new page is loading until the answer asked on that page arrives, as today a newly mounted component was loading until its own fetch answered: giving it the previous page's answer would show a right that may have been removed as current. If that ask fails it gets the fallback, and one retry asks once for every failed component. Components mounted later on the same page reuse that page's answer or failure and ask nothing. Model shared_page_reads.qnt checks this protocol; per-mutant receipts are in design/d10-receipts. The page of each shared read's latest ask, also while it is on its way, is kept in a module-level WeakMap<Query, number> in usePageFreshQuery.ts (pageOfTheLatestAsk), written only by the queryFn when a fetch actually starts. The page-move refresh cancels and then invalidates only the reads whose latest ask belongs to an earlier page (cancel first, because invalidating alone would join a first ask still on its way instead of replacing it); a component that mounted on the new page and already asked is left alone, so a move asks once. This map is allowed module state, unlike the page counter: it is keyed by the TanStack Query object, so it belongs to that cache and query, is collected with it, and cannot leak between QueryClients; it is never written during render, so a StrictMode double render, a StrictMode effect replay or an abandoned concurrent render cannot change it (a fetch that TanStack deduplicates runs the queryFn once). query.meta was rejected because it is static per options, not per fetch, and the query's state has no field the application may write before the answer lands.
